title: Giving a better phone interview ｜ 做好电话面试

sents.en: These days, phone interviews are an unavoidable part of the job interview process, and for good reason: They save time and effort.
sents.cn: 如今，电话面试是求职面试过程中不可避免的一环，这有其充分理由：它省时省力。

sents.en: But that doesn't mean that phone calls require zero energy on the part of the candidate.
sents.cn: 但这并不意味着电话通话对求职者而言无需任何精力。

sents.en: Many companies treat phone screening as the official first round of the hiring process.
sents.cn: 许多公司将电话筛选视为招聘流程正式的第一轮。

sents.en: That means candidates are expected to go into them prepared with as much information as possible about the company, position, and their own skills and strengths.
sents.cn: 这意味着求职者应当尽可能多地了解公司、职位以及自身技能与优势，做好准备后再参加。

sents.en: A big mistake people often make is talking about their personal lives.
sents.cn: 人们常犯的一个大错误是谈论个人生活。

sents.en: Don't talk about your personal life unless you're directly asked a question about what you like to do in your off-hours.
sents.cn: 除非被直接问到闲暇时喜欢做什么，否则不要谈论你的个人生活。

sents.en: "The point of a phone interview is to focus on getting to know a candidate's professional experience and goals," says Mckenzie Roark, campus talent specialist at Lithko Contracting.
sents.cn: "电话面试的重点在于了解求职者的专业经验与目标，"LithkoContracting的校园人才专家麦肯齐∙罗克说。"招聘者想看他们是否最适合某个角色，而了解他们的个人生活并无帮助。

sents.en: "A recruiter is trying to see if they are the best fit for a role, and learning about their personal life doesn't help.
sents.cn: 例如，当被问及五年后你在哪里时，我们不想知道你希望结婚或想买新房。

sents.en: For example, when asked where you see yourself in five years, we don't want to know that you hope to be married or that you want to buy a new house. That is nice, but that isn't relative to anything professional."
sents.cn: 那挺好，但那与任何专业事宜都无关。"

sents.en: It might be tempting to cross something off your to-do list while on a phone interview, but recruiters and hiring managers can easily tell if your attention is elsewhere.
sents.cn: 在电话面试时，你或许很想从待办清单上划掉某件事，但招聘者和招聘经理很容易判断出你的注意力是否在他处。

sents.en: Many interviewers are annoyed to see people who decide to multitask while on the phone interview.
sents.cn: 许多面试官看到有人在电话面试时一心多用，会感到恼火。

sents.en: There are candidates who wash dishes, go for walks, or do grocery shopping during the interview.
sents.cn: 有候选人在面试时洗碗、散步或去杂货店购物。

sents.en: Needless to say, this doesn't reflect well on your level of interest in the position you're interviewing for.
sents.cn: 不用说，这并不能很好地反映你对所面试职位的兴趣程度。

sents.en: The question regarding pay is also best avoided.
sents.cn: 关于薪酬的问题也最好避免。

sents.en: To be frank, it's simply too early in the process for you to be the one who brings up salary expectations.
sents.cn: 坦白说，在流程中由你主动提出薪资期望为时过早。

sents.en: "Chances are if a candidate is participating in a phone interview, this is the first time they have talked with the company, and the first call isn't the appropriate time to talk about 'what's in it for you,'" says Justina Strnad, the Talent Acquisition Manager for Shiftgig.
sents.cn: "如果候选人参加电话面试，这很可能是他们第一次与公司交谈，而第一次通话并不适合谈论'对你有什么好处'，"Shiftgig的人才招聘经理贾斯汀娜∙斯特纳德说。"相信我，如果你是个优秀的候选人并进入下一步，招聘团队之后会就'对你有什么好处'非常透明地说明。

sents.en: "Trust me, if you are a great candidate and make it to the next step, the hiring team is going to be very transparent about what's in it for you later on."
"After wrapping up a phone interview, it is typical that the interviewer will ask the candidate if they have any questions.
sents.cn: "电话面试结束时，面试官通常会问候选人是否有问题。这点我怎么强调都不过分：一定要提问，"罗克说。

sents.en: I can't stress this enough: ALWAYS ask questions," says Roark.
sents.cn: "如果我们进行了一次很棒的电话面试，然后结束时空，他们却对我没有任何问题，这几乎毁了整场面试。

sents.en: "If we have had a great phone interview and then we wrap up and they don't have any questions for me, it pretty much ruins the whole interview.
sents.cn: 这告诉我候选人对这个角色不感兴趣，而事实可能根本不是这样，"她指出。

sents.en: It tells me that the candidate is uninterested in the role, which in reality might not be the case at all," she notes.
sents.cn: 但可以肯定的是，如果你对工作感兴趣，总能想出点什么来问面试官。

sents.en: But surely, if you're interested in a job, you can think of something to ask your interviewer.
It seems basic, but surprisingly, a lot of people are late to phone interviews.
sents.cn: 这看似基本，但令人惊讶的是，许多人对电话面试迟迟不到。

sents.en: "About a quarter of the people with whom I schedule phone interviews aren't on time," says Sophie Cikovsky, who handles U.S. recruiting for Infinite Global.
sents.cn: "与我安排电话面试的人中，约四分之一不准时，"负责InfiniteGlobal美国招聘的索菲∙茨科夫斯基说。"虽然这让我个人困扰，但这也说明此人不太注重细节，"她解释道。

sents.en: "While this bothers me personally, it's also indicative of someone who isn't very detail-oriented," she explains.
sents.cn: "为了在招聘流程早期就识别出这一点，几年前我开始要求所有候选人给我打电话，而不是我在约定时间给他们打。

sents.en: "In order to identify this early in the hiring process, I started asking all candidates a few years ago to call me as opposed to calling them at an agreed-upon time.
sents.cn: 那样的话，如果我在下午1:13或12:49接到他们电话，而不是我们计划的下午1:00面试时间，我就有了一个早期信号：他们可能不太合适。

sents.en: That way, if I hear from them at 1:13 p.m. or 12:49 p.m. instead of our planned 1:00 p.m. interview time, I have an early indicator that they might not be a great fit."
"Make sure you test your headset and connection before dialing in," recommends Roark.
sents.cn: "在拨号前务必测试你的耳机和连接，"罗克建议。

sents.en: "There is nothing more frustrating for a recruiter who has a structured interview guide in place having to repeatedly ask the same question over and over because they could not understand your answer due to dropped signals." Test-call a friend beforehand, or even call yourself from a landline if necessary; it will take less than a minute.
sents.cn: "对一位手头有结构化面试指南的招聘者来说，没有什么比因为信号中断而听不懂你的回答、不得不一遍遍重复同一个问题更令人沮丧的了。"事先给朋友打个测试电话，必要时甚至可以用座机给自己打一个；这用不了一分钟。

sents.en: You might be eager to get your point across or talk about your experience, but interrupting the interviewer is awkward and rude.
sents.cn: 你可能急于表达观点或谈论经验，但打断面试官既尴尬又无礼。

sents.en: "Interviewing can be stressful, and sometimes that stress manifests itself in speaking too fast, speaking too loud, talking over the interviewer, or attempting to answer the interviewer's question before they have actually finished asking the question," says Chris Dardis, a recruiting expert. "Don't do this." There's a big difference between being assertive (自信的) and being aggressive, and interviewers can always recognize it.
sents.cn: "面试可能很有压力，有时这种压力表现为语速过快、声音过大、抢面试官的话，或在面试官还没真正问完问题前就试图回答，"招聘专家克里斯∙达迪斯说。"别这样做。"自信（自信的）与咄咄逼人之间差别很大，而面试官总能分辨出来。

sents.en: It's tough not to say things like "um," "uh," and "like" in everyday speech, but these verbal habits become much more pronounced when speaking on the phone, says Dardis.
sents.cn: 在日常说话中很难不说"嗯""呃""like"这类词，但达迪斯说，在电话交谈时这些言语习惯会变得明显得多。"在面对面面试中，它们没那么显眼，因为还有头发、西装或肢体语言等其他东西分散人们的注意力。

sents.en: "In face-to-face interviews, they're not as noticeable, because there are other things like your hair, suit, or body language to distract people." But in a phone interview, the only thing you have to go on is what you say and how you say it. "That's why it's so important to eliminate these words from your speech when doing a phone interview."
sents.cn: "但在电话面试中，你唯一能依靠的就是你说的话以及你说话的方式。"这就是为什么在电话面试时把这些词从你的言语中剔除如此重要。"

sents.en: Not knowing anything about the company or job you're interviewing for is way more obvious than you'd think.
sents.cn: 对你所面试的公司或职位一无所知，比你想象的要明显得多。"许多人认为他们不必在研究方法或公司上花那么多精力，"人力资源顾问史蒂夫∙普里查德说。如果在面试时你面前摆着笔记本电脑做几次快速搜索，他们不会发现区别，对吧？未必。

sents.en: "Many people think that they don't have to put as much effort into researching the role or the company," says Steve Pritchard, an HR consultant.
sents.cn: "经验丰富的面试官会知道受访者是否在电话中同时做研究。面试官常常甚至能在提问时听到打字声，"他补充道。K)"Thekeytosuccessduringaphoneinterviewisclearandconciseanswers,"saysDardis."People'sattentionspanstendtobeshorteroverthephone.Youdon'twantyourfutureemployertoloseinterestintheconversation."Herecommendspracticinganswerstoquestionsyouknowwillbeaskedaheadoftimeinordertobeclearonwhatyou'regoingtosay.Thatway,youcanpreventtalkinginanaimlessmanner.K）"电话面试成功的关键在于清晰而简洁的回答，"达迪斯说。"人们在电话上的注意力持续时间往往更短。你不会想让你的未来雇主对这场对话失去兴趣。"他建议提前练习那些你知道一定会被问到的问题的答案，以便清楚自己要说什么。
